title: Calls grow for customs reforms to speed up import container clearance - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka's import container clearance process is facing growing criticism, with industry stakeholders urging authorities to implement long-delayed customs reforms to improve efficiency and reduce costs.

Data on imported laden containers handled at the Port of Colombo show that volumes increased from 438,234 TEUs in 2023 to 641,052 TEUs in 2025, marking an increase of 202,818 TEUs or 46.3% over two years.

Despite the sharp growth in import volumes, more than 65% of imported laden containers continue to be selected for physical inspection by Sri Lanka Customs. Industry representatives claim that 88% of the containers inspected were found to be fully compliant with customs regulations, indicating that the current risk management and profiling system requires significant improvement.

They said that many advanced customs administrations inspect only about 20% of import containers, relying instead on intelligence, risk analysis and post-clearance audits to identify high-risk shipments.

According to stakeholders, the current inspection regime has resulted in longer container dwell times, congestion at inspection yards, delays in the delivery of goods, and higher demurrage, detention and transport costs. They argue that these additional expenses are ultimately passed on to consumers while also reducing Sri Lanka's trade competitiveness.

The concerns have already been presented to the Parliamentary Select Committee on Containers, with industry representatives calling for decisive action by the Government, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation, the Director General of Customs, or through a Cabinet-led national reform programme.

They stressed that if Sri Lanka aims to become an international logistics hub, customs procedures must be aligned with international best practices. They argued that reducing unnecessary physical inspections would allow Customs to focus resources on genuinely high-risk cargo, improve the detection of illegal activities, facilitate legitimate trade, lower business costs and ultimately benefit consumers through lower prices.

title: KKS night mail train derails - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - The night mail train travelling from Colombo Fort to Kankesanthurai (KKS) derailed near Senarathgama Railway Station, causing disruptions to services on the Northern railway line.

According to the Railway Department, the train had stopped at Senarathgama Station and, while resuming its journey, two wheels of the locomotive derailed.

As a result of the incident, train operations on the Northern line have been affected. The night mail train travelling from Kankesanthurai to Colombo Fort has been curtailed and will operate only up to Anuradhapura.

Railway officials said a relief train has been dispatched to the site to re-rail the locomotive and restore normal operations. The department expects to complete the recovery work as quickly as possible.

title: Supermarket fined Rs. 500,000 for selling Nadu rice above control price - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - A supermarket in Gampola has been fined Rs. 500,000 after pleading guilty to selling local Nadu rice above the government-controlled maximum retail price, the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) said.

The Kandy District Investigation Officers of the CAA had filed a case before the Gampola Magistrate's Court against Kasagala Green Super Pvt. Ltd., located on Hospital Road, Gampola, for selling local Nadu rice at Rs. 240 per kilogram, exceeding the government-mandated maximum retail price of Rs. 230.

The violation was detected during a raid conducted by CAA investigation officers on June 23, 2026.

When the case was taken up before the Gampola Magistrate's Court on July 14, the company pleaded guilty to the charges. The court subsequently imposed a fine of Rs. 500,000.

The CAA urged consumers to report traders selling food items above the controlled price, as well as substandard or expired products, by contacting its 1977 hotline during office hours.

title: Two Sri Lankans suspected in Wattala shooting detained in India - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Two Sri Lankan nationals suspected of involvement in a shooting incident in Wattala have been detained by Indian Marine Police after allegedly entering India illegally by boat, according to the Hindu.

The two men, identified as 31-year-old G. Vigneswaran and 30-year-old M. Lusinath, both residents of Wattala, were detained after Marine Police personnel on patrol as part of the Sagar Kavach coastal defence exercise spotted them behaving suspiciously along the Dhanushkodi shoreline on Friday.

The duo was taken to the Marine Police Station for questioning, where their identities were established.

During further inquiries, Indian authorities were informed that Sri Lankan authorities suspected the two men of involvement in a shooting incident reported in Wattala on Thursday.

Police sources also said that both men have three pending drug-related cases in Sri Lanka.

Following a request from Sri Lankan authorities for their custody, the suspects were reportedly transferred to a special camp located within the premises of the Tiruchi Central Prison.

They are expected to be repatriated to Sri Lanka within a week, according to police sources.

title: Spanish national arrested at Katunayake Airport with Rs. 110 Mn worth of Cocaine - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Katunayake (July 25 (Daily Mirror) - The Sri Lanka Customs Narcotics Control Unit has arrested a 79-year-old Spanish national after discovering a haul of cocaine valued at nearly Rs. 110 million hidden inside his luggage.

The suspect, identified as an agricultural engineer, arrived in Sri Lanka on July 22. He traveled from Sierra Leone, transiting through Addis Ababa and Doha, before landing at the Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake on Qatar Airways flight QR654.

Upon his initial arrival, customs officials inspected the suspect's hand luggage but found no suspicious items. Because his checked baggage had not arrived on the same flight, authorities permitted him to leave the airport after he completed the necessary arrival formalities.

The delayed baggage subsequently arrived in Sri Lanka, prompting the suspect to return to the airport's arrival terminal at around 6:30 p.m. yesterday (July 24) to claim it. However, before releasing the luggage, Customs Narcotics Control officers subjected it to an X-ray scan.

The scan revealed suspicious materials, leading to a thorough physical inspection of the bag. During the search, officers discovered four parcels of cocaine meticulously concealed within two file folders. The seized narcotics weighed a total of 2.198 kilograms and have an estimated street value of approximately Rs. 109.9 million.

Sri Lanka Customs has initiated a preliminary investigation into the incident. The suspect, along with the seized drugs, is scheduled to be handed over to the Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB) for further investigations and subsequent legal proceedings.

title: Paddy cultivators stage protest in Anuradhapura - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Dayaratne Embogama

Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Paddy cultivators in the Anuradhapura District yesterday staged a protest in Anuradhapura town against the poor guaranteed price for paddy and demanded a minimum price of Rs.150 per kilo.

More than 1,000 farmers affiliated to Nuwarawewa, Nachchaduwa, Thissawewa, Padaviya, Wahalkara, Mahakanadarawa, Huruluwsewa, Rajangana and Wilachchiya farmer organisations participated.

President of Anuradhapura District Farmer Organisation Collective Punchirala Ratnayaka said the farmers staged protests in their areas and, as a last resort, gathered in Anuradhapura to stage this massive protest.

“We made continual representations to the Government, the Minister of Agriculture and Deputy Minister to increase the guaranteed price for paddy but to no avail. We are determined to continue our campaign. The government held talks with the rice mill owners and decided on a guaranteed price of Rs.120, but the rice mill owners pay only Rs. 80 per kilo. Although we had a bumper harvest in the Yala season, we are facing hardship for want of a remunerative market for paddy,” he said.

title: Farewell Ambassador Qi Zhenhong of China! - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Prof. Samitha Hettige

Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka has always been a global trading hub and as result many Envoy appointments are recorded through its long history. Among notable envoys recorded are Emperor Ashoka's Envoys (3rd Century BC), Persian Envoys (2nd Century BC), Roman Envoys (1st Century AD), Chinese Buddhist Scholars (5th Century AD) and Chinese Admiral Zheng He (14th Century AD). Assistance provided by Admiral Zheng He is recorded in the trilingual plaque on display at the national museum in Colombo.

Among notable Sri Lankan Envoys are; trader brothers Thapassu and Balluka (who met the Buddha), Envoys of King Mahanama in China and Rome (1st Century AD) and Ambassador Jayapala of Chilaw in Great China during the Ming Dynasty (14th Century AD). Jayapala is believed to have travelled to China on 6 occasions. It was the peak of the maritime Silk Road when Sri Jayawardenepura became capital under Parakramabahu VI who resided close to ‘Mirihana’ in Jayawardenepura. Above indicates that Sino Lanka diplomatic ties have been stronger than most of Sri Lanka’s bilateral relations.

Term of Ambassador Qi Zhenhong

Ambassador Qi Zhenhong arrived in Sri Lanka in late 2020 when Sri Lanka was combating COVID – 19 under President Gotabaya who ruled the country from Mirihana. Sri Lankans may remember the simple arrival ceremony Chinese Embassy held on advice of Ambassador Qi Zhenhong respecting the health guidelines of Sri Lanka to prevent the spread of COVID – 19.

Ambassador Qi was one of the first to organise free COVID vaccines for Sri Lankans. He will have special memories about Sri Lanka as he witnessed; Sri Lankans fighting COVID -19, mismanaging and re-energising the economy, the peoples uprising (Aragalaya) and the rule of three Executive Presidents. Sri Lankans celebrated the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Peoples Republic of China and Sri Lanka in 2022. In the same year the 70th anniversary of signing the Rubber Rice Pact with China was also marked. China is revisiting the ancient Silk Road for global human development with the four global initiatives (Global Security Initiative, Global Governance Initiative, Global Civilisation Initiative and the Global Development Initiative) supported by the Belt and Road Initiative. As the UN General Assembly has endorsed these initiatives, it is important for Sri Lanka to get more involved with those to re-energise the economy.

Safe journey dear Ambassador!

title: Five people injured after elephant attacks van - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Five people were injured when an elephant attacked a van travelling from Padukka to Anuradhapura yesterday.

It was reported that the van had knocked the animal a few metres before it reached the spot where the tragedy struck.

The injured were admitted to hospital. The condition of three people was said to be serious. Some six people were travelling in the van, according to police.

The village of Padeniya in Anuradhapura District is said to have suffered because of wild elephants during the past few years. Around 20 people have died as a result of human-elephant conflict in the area.

title: Sri Lanka, U.S. discuss collaboration on dengue control measures - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka and the United States have discussed possible collaboration on dengue control measures as the country continues to battle a sharp surge in infections this year.

Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Minister Vijitha Herath said the discussions took place during a meeting with U.S. Ambassador to India and Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor on the sidelines of the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) meeting in Manila, the Philippines, on July 23.

In a post on X, the Minister said the talks focused on strengthening the long-standing bilateral relationship between the two countries, including expanding trade ties.

He added that the two sides also discussed possible collaboration in support of the dengue control measures being undertaken in Sri Lanka.

Sri Lanka is currently facing one of its worst dengue outbreaks in recent years. According to official data, the country had recorded 80,114 dengue cases as of midnight on July 23.

Health authorities have also confirmed 59 dengue-related deaths this year, with a case fatality rate of 0.07%. As of Epidemiological Week 29, there are 175 high-risk Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas, while an average of 2,391 new cases is being reported daily.

The outbreak has escalated significantly in recent days, with 24,739 cases reported in July alone, making it the worst month of the year so far. June recorded 21,534 cases, while the number of infections in earlier months remained comparatively lower.

The Western Province continues to be the epicentre of the outbreak, accounting for more than half of all reported cases nationwide.

Gampaha District has reported 16,950 infections, followed by Colombo with 16,091. Other districts with high case numbers include Matara (5,534), Kandy (4,827), Kalutara (4,545), and Ratnapura (4,428). The Colombo Municipal Council area alone has reported more than 3,200 dengue cases.

title: I will come back to Parliament in 2029 and make sure that Minister Harshana Nanayakkara in prison: Archchuna - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara was asleep after a booze at the time of the clash in Negombo Prison, Independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna alleged in Parliament yesterday.

“The Minister was not aware of what was going on,” he said.

“I will come to Parliament in 2029 as well and will see to it that Minister Nanayakkara is sent to Prison,” he added.

Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe who responded said the Justice Minister having a drink is his personal business. “These MPs speak as if they put soda into the Minister's drink. The Minister performed his duty after the clash. He did everything for the victims of the clash,” he said.

title: Retirement age extension a move nothing but to please Chief Justice: Dayasiri - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - As the government confirmed that an amendment will be introduced to extend the retirement age of judges, one opposition member said it will be made to please the current Chief Justice.

Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekara told Parliament that the constitution amendment is aimed at pleasing Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena.

“This move is named by many as ‘Surasena amendment’, he said while highlighting that the constitution of the country is to be amended just to please one person,” the MP said.

He recalled an instance in the past when the constitution was amended for one Rajadhori, which was called the Rajadhori amendment.

Also, the MP said the President has violated the whole chapter of the constitution on human rights violations. “The claim made by the President that vacancies of upper courts will be filled after filling the vacancies in the lower courts is unacceptable,” he said.

Referring to the recent clash in Negombo Prison, Mr Jayasekara said the incident worsened as there was no one to issue orders. He said the prison police team which was sent to resolve the clash had gone empty-handed. “They did not have rubber bullets or tear gas with them.

Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe, who responded, said an amendment to extend the retirement age of the judges. “There is a fear psychosis among those in the opposition. This is called Surasena fear psychosis,” the Minister said.

The Minister justified the move to extend the retirement age of senior judges, saying such an extension has not been made for a long time.

title: Using unverified home dengue remedies leave patients critically ill - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Some dengue patients have become critically ill after using unverified home remedies, including papaya leaf juice, and have suffered various complications, the Borella National Ayurveda Hospital physician Dr. Saminda Ariyaratne said

He said dengue patients should not use any home remedies other than those prescribed by qualified Western or Ayurvedic doctors.

He also urged the public not to prepare or use medicines based on claims circulating on social media, stressing that only treatments recommended by qualified medical professionals should be followed.

Meanwhile, Dr. Hemachandra said that a special dengue clinic will be opened at the hospital from Friday, July 31, in response to the current dengue outbreak.

He invited patients seeking treatment under the Ayurvedic medical tradition to visit the hospital and receive care from qualified practitioners.

title: Govt. on alert over rising crimes involving foreign nationals - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - The government is on high alert over an increasing number of crimes involving foreign nationals across Sri Lanka, following a recent abduction and murder of a Chinese national linked to a suspected rivalry between Chinese groups in Colombo.

Deputy Minister of Public Security Sunil Watagala told the Daily Mirror that authorities are paying special attention to recent incidents involving foreign nationals and that strict actions are being taken under existing laws.

The Deputy Minister said Sri Lankan authorities remain on high alert following a rise in transnational cybercrime, illegal business operations, and other criminal activities involving foreign nationals.

He made these remarks following a recent crime involving Chinese nationals that resulted in the death of a Chinese citizen. The incident unfolded on Thursday within the high-security Colombo Port City.

The latest case has drawn attention to increasing tensions among foreign groups, with police investigating whether the abduction and murder of a foreign national was connected to a dispute involving cryptocurrency-related activities.

According to police, three Chinese nationals who had arrived at Colombo Port City in a rented cab were ambushed while fishing near the suspension bridge between 2:00 a.m. and 3:00 a.m. on Thursday by around 20 attackers who arrived in a black van. The assailants allegedly threatened them with pistols, tied and blindfolded them, and assaulted them before taking two victims in the van and the third in another vehicle.

The two victims were later abandoned in the van at a Port City parking area, where they freed themselves and reported the incident to Colombo Harbour Police. They were admitted to a private hospital. Hours later, the third victim was found dead in a forested area in Eheliyagoda with severe injuries. Police said the body had been bound, blindfolded, and concealed under stones, and was later identified by the survivors as their missing companion.

During the investigation, police recovered a Glock 44 semi-automatic pistol, a loaded magazine, and a VVK walkie-talkie from the abandoned van. Two Chinese nationals suspected of involvement in the crime were arrested near Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) while allegedly attempting to flee the country.

Meanwhile, Police Spokesman ASP F.U. Wootler said that police suspect that the incident stemmed from a financial dispute between two Chinese groups operating in Sri Lanka. However, he ruled out the involvement of any Sri Lankan nationals in the crime.

He said that two police teams have been deployed to continue investigations and arrest the remaining suspects involved in the attack.

Meanwhile, following the incident, the Chinese Embassy in Colombo said it is closely monitoring the investigation and has urged the Sri Lanka Police to conduct a thorough inquiry, establish the facts as quickly as possible, and safeguard the safety and lawful rights of Chinese citizens in Sri Lanka.

The Embassy also advised Chinese nationals residing in or visiting Sri Lanka to remain vigilant, strengthen their personal safety awareness, promptly report emergencies to the police, and contact the Embassy for consular assistance when necessary.

The incident comes amid increasing concerns about foreign nationals engaging in online financial fraud and telecommunications scam operations while staying in Sri Lanka on tourist visas.

Responding to concerns over visa approvals for foreigners allegedly engaged in illegal activities, Deputy Minister Watagala said the Chinese Embassy in Colombo and Sri Lanka's Department of Immigration and Emigration are closely monitoring the issuance of visas for Chinese nationals travelling to Sri Lanka.

He also said that the Chinese Embassy has, on several occasions, alerted the Sri Lankan government about specific Chinese nationals involved in illegal activities in the country and requested that appropriate action be taken against them.
